title: 1957 AHSME Problem 26
statement: From a point within a triangle, line segments are drawn to the vertices. A necessary and sufficient condition that the three triangles thus formed have equal areas is that the point be:

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: the center of the inscribed circle

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: the center of the circumscribed circle

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
such that the three angles formed at the point each be
\(120^\circ\)

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: the intersection of the altitudes of the triangle

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
the intersection of the medians of the
triangle

solutions.text:
The three medians meet at the centroid and divide the triangle into six small triangles of equal area. Each of the three triangles having the centroid and one side of the original triangle consists of two of those small triangles, so their areas are equal. Conversely, equal areas give equal barycentric coordinates, which uniquely locate the centroid.

Thus, the necessary and sufficient point is the intersection of the medians, and the correct answer is E.
hints: Recall how the medians partition a triangle’s area
The intersection of the medians divides the triangle into six small triangles paired into three equal-area regions
